parties.respondent: M/S NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA

summary: Dispute over interpretation of contract clause regarding measurement method for embankment construction using soil and pond ash. Contractor argued for composite cross-section measurement under BOQ Item 2.02(b) and MoRTH TS Clause 305.8; NHAI and supervising engineer advocated separate measurement. Arbitral tribunal supported contractor's view; single judge upheld award. Division Bench of Delhi High Court set aside the award, finding implausible interpretation. Supreme Court examined scope of judicial interference under Arbitration Act, 1996, emphasizing limited review. Issue centered on whether measurement should be by composite section or segregated by material, with reference to technical specifications, BOQ, and expert interpretations.
legal_provisions_cited: Associate Builders v Delhi Development Corporation
BOC India Ltd. vs. Bhagwati Oxygen Ltd
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, setting aside the judgment of the Division Bench of the Delhi High Court and restoring the arbitral award in favor of the contractor, reaffirming the principle of minimal judicial interference in arbitral awards and upholding the tribunal's plausible interpretation of the contract.
